speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: This reply also addresses another Parliamentary Question (PQ) scheduled for a subsequent Sitting on 17 October.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Members have filed these PQs likely in response to Dyson’s recent retrenchment exercise and I am taking these PQs together to provide a more holistic response.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: To recap, Dyson conducted a retrenchment exercise earlier this month.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Subsequently, the United Workers of Electronics and Electrical Industries (UWEEI) expressed their concern that they were only notified a day before Dyson informed the affected employees.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The Ministry of Manpower (MOM) has been actively involved in this issue and has engaged both parties, who have agreed to work together in the spirit of tripartism.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Members have raised questions on five key issues.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: First, early notification to the union; two, retrenchment benefits; three, mandatory retrenchment notifications; four, action that can be taken against non-compliant companies; and five, how Singapore balances being both pro-business and pro-worker.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I will address each of these issues in the rest of my reply.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: First, Members asked whether the one-day notice in Dyson’s case was sufficient.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Based on the Tripartite Advisory on Managing Excess Manpower or TAMEM, if the company is unionised, it should provide advance notice to the unions.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Where it is provided in the collective agreement, the norm is to notify the union a month before notifying the employees.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We understand that all the retrenched employees from Dyson are professionals, managers or executives (PMEs) who are not unionised.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: At the same time, the spirit of tripartite engagements is built on trust and a shared understanding between the employer and the union.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: It is good practice for companies to do so, as this builds trust between the employer and the union.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Dyson has explained to UWEEI the reasons for not being able to give more advance notice to the union.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Communications are key to managing the concerns of the affected employees, while also being cognisant of the constraints of businesses.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: In this respect, both parties have committed to continue working together in the tripartite spirit to support both the needs of workers and businesses.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: To work together effectively, trust between the union and employer is key.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This trust cannot be taken for granted and it needs to be built up over time.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Companies should value Singapore’s tripartite culture and work closely with the unions.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: At the same time, the unions also need to do their part to manage the concerns of employees, while recognising business needs.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This is the delicate balance that has made our model of tripartism work well over the years.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Ultimately, it is also important that all tripartite partners focus on the welfare of the affected workers, so that we can work together to help them during this difficult period of disruption.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Second, Members asked about the compensation for the retrenched workers.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Retrenchment benefits are payments made by a company to provide some financial support to help the affected workers through the period of disruption.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Based on the Tripartite Advisory, the amount of retrenchment benefits depends on what is provided in the collective agreement, otherwise it will be negotiated.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Based on our tripartite guidelines, the retrenchment benefits for PMEs can be calculated differently from that for a rank-and-file employee.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: In addition, only employees that have served the company for at least two years are eligible for retrenchment benefits, but Dyson provided affected employees who have served for less than two years a payment as well.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, that goes beyond what they are obliged to do.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: In addition, Dyson will also provide after-care support, outplacement assistance and access to career coaching and counselling to the affected employees.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Separately, Members have asked about the salaries of the affected employees.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: As a policy, we do not disclose salary details as these remain confidential to the employee and company.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Third, Members asked about Dyson’s submission of the mandatory retrenchment notification (MRN).

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Dyson submitted its MRN to MOM on time, within five working days of notifying the affected employees.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This has enabled the Taskforce for Responsible Retrenchment and Employment Facilitation (RTF) to work with Dyson to provide career facilitation services and information kits to the affected employees.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Members also had questions about the MRN requirement more generally.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Among the late submissions, around half were submitted before the retrenchment date of the affected employees.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This means that the RTF is still able to offer employment assistance to affected employees in a timely manner.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: On whether MRNs should be submitted earlier, we need to strike a balance between allowing employers sufficient time to finalise their decisions, while enabling the prompt provision of career facilitation services and programmes to affected employees.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Employers may need more time to decide on how they want to restructure and transform their business and at the same time, collate details required on the affected workers for MRN submission.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Nonetheless, employers can provide early notification to MOM, if they are considering an upcoming retrenchment exercise and rest assured, we will treat the information that we receive sensitively.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Employers can access this early notification channel on the MOM website, to obtain more assistance on how to conduct a responsible retrenchment exercise and provide earlier employment assistance to the affected workers.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Fourth, Members asked about the action that can be taken towards non-compliant companies.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Today, Mr Speaker, most employers follow our retrenchment regulations.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Workers, including PMEs, who are not covered by a collective agreement with the union, can still seek the union’s assistance to be represented individually.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: They may also approach the Tripartite Alliance for Dispute Management (TADM) who can assist if there are contractual or salary disputes, TAFEP if unfair or discriminatory practices were conducted, as well as Workforce Singapore and the National Trades Union Congress's (NTUC's) Employment and Employability Institute (e2i) for employment assistance.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Most employers are cooperative when approached by TAFEP or MOM.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This shows that our tripartite guidelines and advisories are working well without the need for additional penalties, which may negatively affect the wider business environment in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Fifth, Members have asked how Singapore can continue to be pro-business, while safeguarding the welfare of workers.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Businesses need flexibility to make decisions, which will allow them to adapt to market conditions and transform their business models.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Singapore is currently ranked first in the 2024 IMD World Competitiveness Ranking.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We need to constantly maintain a fine and delicate balance in preserving our economic competitiveness, which in turn results in more job opportunities and good wages for our workers.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This is how we keep our long-term unemployment rate low.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Real wages have also consistently improved over the past decade.
There are other countries where the labour market is more rigid or where there is a more confrontational relationship between the unions and the employers.
This makes a country less attractive for companies to invest in.
So, we have to strike a balance between protecting workers and providing flexibility for businesses.
If we do not get this balance right, we may think that we are protecting our workers in the short term.

But in the longer term, the good jobs for our workers may be reduced as we become a less attractive place for companies to invest in and firms may choose to site their operations or even outsource jobs elsewhere.
Together with our tripartite partners, we work upstream to help companies and their workforce upskill, transform and even redesign jobs to improve talent retention, workforce productivity and wages.
We will continue to help workers to build career resilience through picking up industry-relevant skillsets.
This enables our workers to find new and better opportunities, even in the event of a retrenchment.
Workers affected by retrenchment are assisted through employment facilitation and career coaching.
From 2025, the SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support Scheme will further help involuntarily unemployed persons to bounce back.
We need to continue achieving the right balance between the interests of the businesses while ensuring that our workers remain protected and well supported during this difficult period of disruption.
Trust and a shared understanding among our tripartite partners is key for Singapore to manage this balance well, so that Singapore remains pro-worker and pro-business at the same time.
Our strong tripartite spirit will enable Singapore to remain exceptional and achieve continued economic success.
This will in turn ensure that our workers get good jobs and wages for many decades to come.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Can I declare that I have Clementi residents, some of whom are NTUC brothers and sisters, who feel disquiet at how some recent retrenchments have been conducted.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Can I ask the Senior Minister of State two sets of supplementary questions?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: It was a high signature opening, with the then-Prime Minister of Singapore Mr Lee Hsien Loong in attendance.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Can I ask the Senior Minister of State, firstly, given that it was a high-profile company accorded highest recognition, should there be some consideration as to whether such a firm should be benchmarked against the minimum legal standard of what is acceptable?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Or whether such firms can have a higher level of ambition in a situation of retrenchments, so as to better support workers to notify the union earlier and thereby, strengthen tripartism and strengthen the firm's reputation as well as a good employer?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: And, if so, has MOM considered how such norms might be eroded when companies do not fully respect tripartite best practices during a retrenchment?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: And would MOM agree that the next company with retrenchment plans will be watching how this is conducted and that there is a potential risk that such norms can be eroded gradually and then suddenly, and we have to reinforce tripartism at every step?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We see that the unions are at the forefront in negotiating collective agreements and ensuring that our workers are protected.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We also have existing regulations, laws, rules and advisories of which there are multiple layers.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: They have also covered workers with less than two years' experience, even though the advisories do not require it.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: They have also provided counselling as well as outplacement assistance.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: And these are, I think, areas in which good employers also try to help those affected.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But certainly, I know the unions want to do more for their workers.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: They want to ensure that all workers are protected, they want to ensure that the PMEs are also protected and therefore, the alarms were raised.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: MOM stepped in, had the two parties discuss and at the end of the day, tripartism prevailed.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: And that is why, we are unlike other countries where you have lawsuits, you have strikes and you erode the confidence of the business community.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: In terms of how we handle things here in Singapore, I think that is the difference between our approach and that of most parts of the world.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I think there are very few countries that you find the government stepping in, and unions and employers coming to a consensus.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Certainly, I have to thank UWEEI for also holding that ground and Dyson for stepping forward and doing more for workers too.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, I think what we want is a win-win outcome on both sides.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But there are areas that we can improve.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: If there is one thing, we also find that the norm is for many companies to work with the unions and inform them a month early, hence, for example, this is potentially one area.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The union raised concerns that they were only given a one-day notice, although Dyson has also informed them why this particular situation had certain considerations.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We understand that businesses in general have other considerations, especially listed companies.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: In giving too early a notice, they have to tell the shareholders, to give market notice and it is very odd that one already informed the unions before informing the market.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I am not saying that these are specific to Dyson, but generally, there are different considerations on why companies do that.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Therefore, in my reply, trust between employers, unions and the Government is ultimately very important.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: That we will be able to support them despite their commercial or business constraints or considerations while at the same time still maintaining tripartism at its best.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I think this is one area in which I agree with the Member that certainly, we have to preserve this spirit of tripartism to make Singapore work.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Given the recent retrenchment exercise, how does the Ministry measure the effectiveness of current protocols in terms of protecting workers interests?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: And beyond just the timing of notifications, how does the Ministry encourage companies to communicate more transparently with employees and unions during retrenchment processes?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: And could more structured dialogues between companies, employees and unions be considered part of the tripartite guidelines and best practices?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Certainly, we try to do our best in terms of managing the business constraints and business needs, as I have shared.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: And I think today, we are fortunate enough that the economy is doing okay, in the sense that when you look at the unemployment rates, they are low.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: If you look at the retrenchment numbers, they are not far off, they are about the same as non-recession cycles.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I think that is one way in which we look at the macro picture.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But, of course, on the ground, that is where the rubber hits the road, and where you find many of our schemes and layers of protections that we have for our workers.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Having said that, as I have shared in my earlier reply, you also have TAFEP.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Should workers feel that there are discriminatory practices, you can come to us and we will look into these cases.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: There is TADM, if there are contractual disputes, including on retrenchment benefits, we will deal with them through TADM.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: And of course, upstream, we focus on career facilitation, in terms of job matching and career counselling.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: And let us not forget, we can work with employers better too, in terms of some of the restructuring and job redesign efforts, in which there are programmes such as Career Conversion Programmes, through which we can help employers place workers and help redesign jobs so that they do not get retrenched, they can get redeployed into other roles.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: And you can also try out workers in various new functions too and all are subsidised and supported by the Government and the unions through the company training committees.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, we do have multiple means of support for workers, both downstream and upstream, to ensure that our workers are not just protected, but also supported.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We hope that we maintain the economy in a good space, on an even keel, so that we can always ensure that workers have good opportunities and good jobs.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Just one supplementary question and a point of clarification.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: And just a point clarification on his earlier comment that sometimes this is market-sensitive information, but in my many years with the Labour Movement and handling numerous retrenchments, there are many listed companies that, because of the very strong labour management relationship, do keep unions informed, sometimes even three months or six months in advance, although they are listed companies, whether locally or globally.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I think it is important that we continuously look at our practices and guidelines to make sure that they are relevant and, from time to time, issues like this crop up.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: For example, what is an appropriate notification period and businesses will say that they have commercial sensitivities.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: And yes, there are some who will give early notice and some less so.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: It is down to trust that you have to build and manage over time.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Some of these are new firms that have just invested into Singapore and therefore need time versus others who have been here for much longer.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: And as tripartite partners, we need to also open up constant communications between all parties, where both may find certain parts of our regulations or advisories to be outdated over time and need to be updated to deal with new or current issues.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I think we need to just continue those conversations and dialogues.
